description: 🧵 CLI tool for directly patching container images!

summary.one_liner: Copa is a Go CLI that directly patches OS package vulnerabilities in existing container images without a full rebuild, using vulnerability scan reports or package metadata.
summary.what_it_does: Copa takes an existing container image and applies package updates as an extra patch layer, using buildkit to write the result. It can read vulnerability reports from scanners such as Trivy to decide which packages to update, or run a comprehensive update from package metadata in the image. Updates are obtained through the relevant package-manager tooling or Chisel release definitions, and the README says new adapters can be added for more package managers and report formats. The README also describes support for Ubuntu Chiseled images: full-status images support report-driven and comprehensive updates, while native Chisel images with /var/lib/chisel/manifest.wall support comprehensive updates only, with --chisel-release to select a release. The README states that Trivy v0.69.3 does not extract OS package inventory from native manifest.wall files.
use_cases: patch OS package vulnerabilities in container images without rebuilding
apply scanner-reported fixes to third-party images
patch inherited base image vulnerabilities faster than waiting for upstream
add a remediation step after Trivy vulnerability scans
reduce redistribution size of patched images with a small patch layer
notable: Patches existing images without requiring the publisher to change their build
Can work from vulnerability scanner reports or from package metadata in the image
Adds a patch layer rather than rebuilding, so layer hashes of the original image are preserved
Supports native Chisel manifest.wall images with --chisel-release, including public HTTPS Git URLs pinned to a commit or tag
caveats: Trivy does not extract OS package inventory from native Chisel manifest.wall files (verified with Trivy v0.69.3), and native manifest images support only comprehensive updates
Chisel support initially uses public archives only
